records.distractors: Ignoring tension gives g=10. Dividing by only the mass difference would give a different or excessive acceleration; T=16 N is neither an acceleration nor either individual resultant.
records.manualArithmetic: With opposite local positive directions, Mg−T=MA and T−mg=mA. A=10·3/5=6 m/s². T=1(10+6)=4(10−6)=16 N; the individual resultants are 24 and 6 N.
records.physicalAssumptions: Fixed ideal massless frictionless pulley; taut massless inextensible rope; inertial laboratory; uniform exact g=10 m/s². Constant masses satisfy M>m>0. Only weight and tension act, before any end stop. Opposite positive local directions give the same acceleration modulus, 0<A<g, with mg<T<Mg. Eliminating T uses oriented scalar equations, not opposite Cartesian tensions: both actual tension vectors point upwards.
